data.name: Sereliah
data.gender_notes: Sereliah is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Sereliah is derived from the Hebrew word 'ser' meaning 'rule' or 'prosperity' and 'el' meaning 'God'. This name is biblical, referenced in the Old Testament as the name of a Levite priest who ministered in the temple during the reign of King Hezekiah (1 Chronicles 6:14). It can also symbolize God's provision, rule, or prosperity.
data.etymology: Sereliah belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's provision, rule, or prosperity.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sereliah total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

historical_references.reference: The prophet Serah or Serahiah is mentioned in the Old Testament Book of Numbers (10:29-30) as the sister of Moses and Aaron. She is also called Miriam's sister, making her the elder sister of Moses. When the Israelites left Egypt, she was a part of the band of musicians who accompanied the Israelites' journey out of Egypt.

Seraliah is also mentioned in the New Testament Book of Ezra (8:1-36) as a son of the high priest Ezra, born during the Babylonian Captivity. He is one of the names of the priestly families who returned to Jerusalem to rebuild the temple.
